November 1, 2026

Iran says Su-35 contract with Russia is signed, delivery to follow the war

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

IRGC spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Iran's contracts for Russian Su-35 fighter jets are signed and its pilots have been trained, with delivery expected after the war, according to The Jerusalem Post. The jets were reportedly due to arrive before the war began. Russia has not confirmed the claim. Iran's air force currently flies mostly pre-1979 U.S. aircraft and older Russian models.

US federal debt passes the size of the economy for the first time since World War II

tags: economy, politics
sources: @groundnews

Publicly held federal debt reached $32.4 trillion as of September 30, exceeding the $32.2 trillion of gross domestic product recorded over the preceding year. Total federal debt including intragovernmental holdings surpassed $40.5 trillion this week, up from $36.2 trillion at the start of President Donald Trump's second term. The Congressional Budget Office projects publicly held debt will reach 120% of GDP by 2036, above the post-World War II record of 106% in 1946, with the 2025 tax and spending law projected to add $4.7 trillion through 2035.

ICE paid $495.6 million for a Minnesota prison offered to the state for $75 million

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @groundnews

An investigation by KARE 11 found that Immigration and Customs Enforcement paid $495.6 million in August for a vacant Minnesota prison whose owner had offered it to the state for $75 million in May 2025. The facility, closed for 16 years, was bought to expand detention capacity under the administration's immigration crackdown, and private operator CoreCivic, which gave $500,000 to the president's inaugural fund, secured an operating contract estimated at $75 million a year. Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison called for a congressional investigation. CoreCivic said independent appraisers assessed the property and the federal government set the final price, while a federal watchdog has warned that ICE prison purchases risk wasting taxpayer money.

Judge dismisses Trump's Epstein letter lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal with prejudice

tags: legal, media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A judge threw out President Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal over its publication of a 50th birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein that Trump says he did not write. The ruling found the complaint did not sufficiently plead actual malice, and was issued with prejudice, meaning the case cannot be refiled. The judge also raised the question of attorney's fees, which Trump may be ordered to pay in part.

Congo Ebola outbreak death toll passes 5,000

tags: health
sources: @oafnation_actual

Congo's health ministry reported 5,026 deaths out of 10,351 infections, a lethality rate close to 50 percent. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus and declared in mid-May, has spread to 67 health zones across eight provinces. It is now the second deadliest Ebola outbreak on record, behind the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic.

Pentagon starting near zero on mass drone production, innovation chief says

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

Acting Defense Innovation Unit chief Travis Metz told Bloomberg the Pentagon is beginning from essentially nothing on mass-producing cheap military drones. Its Drone Dominance Program targets roughly 250,000 drones by the end of 2027, backed by about $1.1 billion. Ukrainian intelligence estimates Russia will build 7.3 million small drones this year.

FBI found some evidence in 2016 Ilhan Omar marriage inquiry but brought no charges

tags: immigration, legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

A New York Times report says the FBI found some evidence supporting allegations that Rep. Ilhan Omar entered a fraudulent marriage to obtain immigration benefits, and that the 2016 investigation ended without charges because prosecutors believed the statute of limitations had expired. Omar has denied marrying her brother, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, for immigration purposes and has called the claims a racist conspiracy theory; a 2019 Minneapolis Star Tribune investigation could neither confirm nor disprove the alleged relationship. The report follows a separate federal investigation in which Omar's Washington home was searched on October 12. President Donald Trump has raised the possibility of deporting Omar, and no charges have been announced.

Democrats hold a 343,000-vote early voting edge in North Carolina

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Early voting figures from North Carolina show Democrats with a 343,000-vote registration advantage in 2026, compared with a 41,000-vote Republican advantage at the close of early in-person voting in 2024. Republicans did not lead on any single day of early voting, with gains among high-propensity Republican voters outweighed by turnout among less frequent Democratic voters. The figures do not indicate how those ballots were cast.

Members of Congress prepare investigations into Trump and his family ahead of midterms

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Members of Congress are preparing wide-ranging investigations of President Donald Trump and his children, with one member saying Eric Trump, Donald Trump Jr. and Barron Trump are at the top of her list. Advisers reportedly warn that a Democratic win could leave the president, in insiders' words, the lamest of lame ducks, facing a Congress focused on investigations and a court system issuing repeated rebukes. Attention inside the White House is also said to be turning toward 2028 and a potential presidential run by the vice president.

Judge rejects Trump bid to delay certification of Alaska Senate race

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A judge dismissed a lawsuit brought by President Donald Trump seeking to delay certification of the Alaska Senate race. The ruling means certification will not be blocked or postponed, at least for now.

Trump ordered to produce discovery in $10 billion BBC lawsuit or face dismissal

tags: legal, media
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge ordered President Donald Trump to hand over critical discovery documents in his $10 billion lawsuit against the BBC by November 23. If the deadline is missed, the court indicated the case will be dismissed. Trump would then be responsible for the costs associated with the suit.

Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers as staff resign

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Rep. Haley Stevens appeared at a Detroit church with Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers and endorsed him, prompting most of her staff, including her chief of staff, to resign, according to the Detroit News. Stevens had said after losing the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed that she would support the Democratic nominee and ticket. El-Sayed responded by saying he does not think about Stevens, and pivoted to affordability, health care costs, local control of schools and union rights, criticizing Rogers's record on prescription drug prices and labor.

New York enacts restrictions on AI chatbots interacting with children

tags: tech, legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Gov. Kathy Hochul signed legislation barring AI chatbots from certain behaviors when interacting with users under 18, including pretending to have human emotions or relationships, using flattery, encouraging secrecy or unhealthy behavior, and generating sexually explicit content. The law allows the state attorney general to sue developers, with penalties including financial damages, chatbot shutdowns and data destruction. Jim Steyer of Common Sense Media, which backed the bill, called it the strongest kids' AI safety bill in the country. The measure comes as states expand AI regulation amid limited congressional action and opposition from President Donald Trump.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins draws condemnation over official post

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A post from the official account of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins drew widespread criticism, with commenters describing its content as openly racist. The post was published from the cabinet member's verified government account.

Trump posts AI-generated video of a US military base in Greenland days before the election

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated video depicting the United States building a military base across Greenland, captioned as a welcome to Greenland. The post came three days before Election Day.

Trump closes campaign with claims of record poverty and jobs numbers

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Asked for his final message to voters, President Donald Trump said individual income is the highest it has ever been and that poverty numbers are the best on record. He also said the country has more people working than at any point in its history, that the military is the strongest it has been, and that manufacturing is returning.

Trump touts wealthy guests at Mar-a-Lago Halloween party on election eve

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

President Donald Trump hosted a Halloween party at Mar-a-Lago featuring caviar and told reporters he has many rich members and that all of Wall Street was present. The event came days before an election in which affordability has been a central issue. Critics characterized the remarks as a let-them-eat-cake moment.

Republican in Iowa attack ad has child endangerment conviction, report finds

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Shellie Flockhart, a Republican city councilwoman featured in a campaign ad attacking Democratic candidate Sarah Trone Garriott in a competitive Iowa House race, has a criminal record involving child endangerment, according to The Washington Post. In the ad, Flockhart criticizes Garriott's record on issues involving children and says she is plain dangerous when it comes to kids. Flockhart pleaded guilty to charges from a 2017 incident in which authorities said she drove under the influence of alcohol with two of her children in the vehicle, including child endangerment and driving under the influence.

Heckler confronts Ken Paxton over bribery allegations at Texas campaign event

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Texas Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton asked supporters at a campaign event to explain the difference between himself and Democrat James Talarico. An attendee responded by shouting that Paxton takes bribery, referring to allegations against him.

Scientists edit DNA inside the human body for the first time using prime editing

tags: health, tech
sources: @groundnews

Biotechnology company Prime Medicine administered an experimental prime editing treatment to a patient with Wilson disease, a genetic disorder in which copper accumulates in the liver and damages organs. The treatment targets mutations in the ATP7B gene that prevent liver cells from clearing excess copper, and unlike standard CRISPR methods, prime editing can rewrite, insert or delete DNA sequences. The trial marks a step toward editing genes inside patients rather than modifying extracted cells in a laboratory, with initial results expected in 2027.

Business jet crashes in Palm Beach County, Florida

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A business jet crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, according to preliminary analysis by authorities, leaving a crater at the site. Video taken by a bystander captured the moment of impact. No casualty figures had been released.
